title: Kid Ory recordings of 1947 and 1949
summary: Redd details the 1947 Vault date at the Rendezvous Ballroom and the 1949 Beverly Cavern live recording.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: 1947 on the Vault label, recorded at the Rendezvous Ballroom in Culver City. This was a very informal record date; in

fact, the musicians were not aware that they were recording. Someone in the audience was again, illegally taping and in the late fifties, it seems that this Vault recording showed up in Europe. The personnel on that date was the legendary Kid Ory on trombone; Ed, Montudie, Garland on bass; Ram Hall on drums; Joe Darensbourg, clarinet; Buster Wilson, piano; Bud Scott, banjo.

The songs recorded were 'Mahogany Hall Stomp', 'Do What Ory Says', 'My Gal Sal', 'Maryland, My Maryland', 'A La Ba', an old creole song, 'Tiger Rag', 'Didn't He Ramble', 'Down Home Rag', 'South' and 'Dipper Mouth Blues.'

1949, the label Sound Records. This date was recorded live at the Beverly Cavern in Los Angeles. The personnel included, in addition to Kid Ory, Mr. Blakeney Ed Garland--Montudie that was--; Ram Hall; Joe Darensbourg; Buster Wilson; Bud Scott and on four of the tracks, Teddy Buckner.
The sides in which Mr. Blakeney

appeared were entitled, 'I'm Busy and You Can't Come In;' 'Wang Wang Blues;' 'Down in Jungletown;' 'Tuxedo Junction;' 'The World is Waiting for the Sunrise;' 'After You're Gone;' 'I'll Be With You Where You Are.' The other trumpet /tracks featured Teddy Buckner on compositions 'Shine,' 'Ball in' The Jack,' 'I Found A New Baby.' This was a live recording from the nightclub Beverly Caverns on the Sound Record Label.
